title: Architecture Standards Codex: API, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance, and ADRs
author: Evelyn Chen
body:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's core architecture and engineering standards for API design, coding conventions, infrastructure, model-serving, observability, and performance. It is intended as the canonical reference for design reviews, ADRs, and day-to-day implementation decisions. Where possible, standards include rationale, measurable thresholds (SLOs), ownership, and links to ADRs or implementation playbooks.

Scope and audience
- Audience: engineers (backend, infra, ML infra), product, SRE, and security reviewers.
- Scope: new services, major refactors, model-onboarding pipelines, public API changes, and infra provisioning.

1) API Standards
Purpose: predictable, stable APIs enable client integrations, versioning, and rollout safety.

Principles
- Consistency: use REST + JSON for public-facing endpoints and gRPC for internal high-throughput RPCs.
- Explicit versioning: include /v{major}/ in all public endpoints. Major version bumps require an ADR and migration plan.
- Semantic URLs: resources, not verbs (e.g., POST /v1/outputs, GET /v1/models/{model_id}/metrics).
- Idempotency: mutation endpoints must support an idempotency key header X-Idempotency-Key.
- Authentication: Bearer tokens (short-lived) + mTLS for private deployments.
- Error model: use structured error object {code:string, message:string, details:optional}. HTTP status mapping: 4xx client, 5xx server.

API change process
1. Create API design doc in PR including request/response examples and migration plan.
2. Add tests for backward-compatibility.
3. Reviewer checklist: contract tests, load test for endpoints, and a monitoring dashboard.
4. Publication: update SDKs and release notes prior to reachability.

Example contract (JSON)
- Request: POST /v1/generate
  {
    "model": "redwood-1",
    "input": "Hello",
    "max_tokens": 256
  }
- Response: 200
  {
    "id": "req_123",
    "output": "Hello world",
    "usage": { "tokens": 5 }
  }

2) Coding and API Implementation Standards
Guidelines
- Languages: Go for high-throughput services, Python for orchestration and ML utilities, TypeScript for frontend/admin UI.
- Code style: follow gofmt/golangci-lint for Go; black + ruff for Python; eslint + prettier for TS.
- API handlers: keep thin controllers, move business logic into services, and database access into repositories.
- Input validation: use schema validation (OpenAPI/JSON Schema). Reject early with clear error codes.
- Secrets: no secrets in code or checked-in config. Use KMS for private deployment and Vault for hosted systems.

Testing requirements
- Unit tests >= 90% coverage for service-layer code.
- Integration tests for API contracts that run in CI on PRs.
- Contract tests for public endpoints that run against a staging API.

3) Infrastructure Standards
Principles
- Declarative infra only: Terraform for cloud, Helm + Kustomize for Kubernetes manifests.
- Environment parity: dev -> staging -> prod parity for feature flags & config.
- Network: least-privilege security groups and VPC per environment for isolation.

Provisioning table (minimum requirements)
| Component | Minimum Config | Purpose | Owner |
|----------|----------------|---------|-------|
| API gateway | 2x AZ + WAF | Ingest public traffic | infra-team |
| Control plane DB | R/W replicas, backups daily | configuration/state | infra-team |
| GPU serving pool | autoscaling GPUs (min 2), Taint:gpu=true | model inference | serving-runtime |

Secrets management
- Hosted: AWS KMS + Secrets Manager; Rotate keys every 90 days.
- Private: customer-managed HSM supported; document procedure in onprem-packaging.

4) Model-Serving Standards
Goals: predictable latency, efficient GPU utilization, safe rollouts and quality guardrails.

Model packaging
- Model manifest: every model must include model.yaml with fields: model_id, architecture, tokenizer, quantization_profile, expected_min_latency_ms (p90), memory_requirements_mb.

Serving runtime requirements
- KV cache support for chat sessions.
- Dynamic batching with latency SLAs. Batching policy configurable per-model.
- Quantization profiles stored in quantization-profiles catalog.

Rollout and compatibility
1. Canary: 1% traffic against new model variant for 24h.
2. Evaluate: automated evals on predefined prompt set + live quality sampling.
3. Promote: 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated rollback triggers.

Quality gates (automated)
- Latency: p95 must not exceed model_manifest.expected_min_latency_ms * 1.5.
- Error rate: 5xx per-minute should not increase by >50% over baseline.
- Quality regression: automatic A/B eval comparing BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity thresholds or custom task metrics.

5) Observability Standards
What to collect
- Traces: distributed traces for request paths (OpenTelemetry).
- Metrics: per-endpoint latency (p50/p95/p99), error rate, throughput, GPU utilization, batch sizes.
- Logs: structured JSON logs with trace_id, span_id, request_id, model_id, route.

SLOs and alerting
- API availability (hosted): 99.95% monthly.
- API latency: p95 < 300ms for small text gen calls (<=128 tokens), p95 < 1.2s for medium calls (<=1024 tokens).
- Serving SLOs tracked per-model and per-customer for Dedicated/Private tiers.

Alert thresholds (examples)
- High error rate: overall 5xx rate > 0.5% for 5m -> P1 page.
- Latency degradation: 30% increase in p95 vs. baseline for 10m -> P2 alert.
- GPU saturation: GPU utilization > 90% for 10m with growing queue -> P2.

Dashboards and runbooks
- Every service must ship a Grafana dashboard with panels for latency, errors, throughput, and downstream dependencies.
- Include targeted runbooks for common alerts (link to runbooks folder).

6) Performance Standards and Benchmarks
Benchmarking requirements
- Perf suite: benchmarking-and-perf-suite runs nightly for core models and weekly for the full catalog.
- Load testing: before a major release, run k6 or Fortio scenario approaching 1.5x expected peak QPS.

Performance budgets (example)
- Per-token CPU/GPU latency: track tokens/ms and maintain historical baselines.
- Cost targets: target median cost per 1k tokens (internal metric) per model family.

Optimization checklist
1. Verify batch sizes and batching window don't violate latency SLOs.
2. Ensure prefix caching for repeated prompts.
3. Apply quantization profile where quality/regression tests pass.
4. Tune kernel selection and apply runtime compilation flags.

7) ADR Process and Key Decisions
Policy
- Significant architecture changes must be recorded as an ADR. An ADR template is available in the ADRs folder. ADRs should include: decision, context, alternatives considered, pros/cons, and follow-up tasks.

Notable ADRs (examples)
- ADR-2025-02: Adopt Go for high-throughput inference control plane.
- ADR-2025-09: Use gRPC for internal model-streaming paths.
- ADR-2026-01: Standardize on OpenTelemetry for tracing.

ADR workflow
1. Draft ADR and propose in architecture-and-standards channel.
2. Add reviewers (SRE, infra, serving-runtime, security). 2 approvers required.
3. Publish and link ADR to implementation tickets.

8) Ownership and Governance
- Standards owner: Architecture Guild (rotating leads from serving-runtime, infra, and eng-platform). Contact: arch-guild@redwood.ai.
- Review cadence: quarterly reviews of standards and annual audit of ADRs and compliance.

Appendix A: Checklist for Reviews (pre-merge)
- API contract tests: PASS
- Load test: PASS for expected QPS
- Security review: secrets, auth, and network rules reviewed
- Observability: traces, metrics, logs instrumented
- ADR created if major change: LINK/ADDED

Appendix B: Example model.yaml (required fields)
```
model_id: redwood-1
architecture: transformer-xl
tokenizer: bpe-v0
quantization_profile: q4_0
expected_min_latency_ms: "120"
memory_requirements_mb: "16384"
owner_team: serving-runtime
support_slo: "p95<300ms"
```

Appendix C: Links and references
- ADR template: confluence/architecture-and-standards/adr-template
- Observability standards: confluence/architecture-and-standards/observability-standards
- Model onboarding: confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding
